commentary.heading: Wall Street mixed as Nvidia slips despite strong results
commentary.body: US shares finished mixed on Wednesday. The S&P 500 eased 0.23% to 7,323.6, its fifth straight fall, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.42% to 24,429.9 and the Dow lost 561 points (1.1%). Nvidia's revenue more than doubled from a year earlier to US$115.8 billion, but its shares closed 2.7% lower amid leadership uncertainty and a delayed quarterly filing. Health insurers dragged the Dow after a proposed government anti-fraud rule, with UnitedHealth and Humana each down about 6%.

commentary.heading: ASX falls for a fifth day
commentary.body: The ASX 200 dropped 0.69% to 8,821.8 on Wednesday, with nine of 11 sectors lower. Technology was weakest, down 2.3%, as TechnologyOne fell 6.1% and Xero 3.8%. Materials lost 1.1% as gold, silver and copper prices retreated: Evolution Mining fell 5.3% and Rio Tinto 1.7%. Lendlease slumped about 17%. Energy was the best sector, up 0.5%. Wage data showed pay rising 1.1% in the September quarter and 3.5% over the year.

commentary.heading: Asia steadies, London slides on miners
commentary.body: Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 0.91% to 23,294.8, with JD.com down 7.2% after its results missed expectations. Mainland shares edged higher, the Shanghai Composite up 0.09% to 3,587.8 and the Shenzhen Component up 0.20% to 10,659.4, as technology themes stabilised during the APEC summit in Shenzhen. In London the FTSE 100 fell 1.30% to 10,551.2 as sharp falls in metal prices hit miners such as Antofagasta, Anglo American and Glencore.

commentary.heading: Central banks and inflation
commentary.body: UK inflation rose to 3.6% in October from 3.5%, a little below forecasts, with core inflation steady at 2.8%. Minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed almost all officials saw further rate rises as likely, and a couple raised the idea of a move larger than a quarter point. The US federal funds range remains 3.75–4.00%, the RBA cash rate 4.85% and the Bank of England rate 4.00%.

commentary.heading: Bonds, oil and the Australian dollar
commentary.body: Yields eased. The US 10-year Treasury fell to about 5.07%, the UK 10-year dropped 9 basis points to 5.30% after the softer-than-expected inflation figure, and Australia's 10-year slipped to 5.09%. US crude fell about 3% to US$82.08 a barrel as US stockpiles rose, and gold dropped about 3.5%. The Australian dollar weakened to around 67.1 US cents, its lowest level since mid-January.

commentary.heading: What to watch
commentary.body: Australia's October jobs figures are out today, after the unemployment rate reached 4.7% in September. Anthropic's shares are due to begin trading on the Nasdaq tonight, and Walmart reports results. China sets its loan prime rates on Friday. Further ahead, the RBA meets on 8 December and the Fed on 9 December.
